problem: The text says a small buzzer may draw 'under about 30 mA' and that 'a pin can drive them'. Section 1 of the same chapter says to keep an Arduino pin at or below 20 mA. A student who follows the buzzer sentence will drive a pin past the limit the chapter itself set, which is the exact mistake the LED section warns against.
fix: Say: small buzzers that draw under about 20 mA can be driven from a pin directly; anything that draws more (many buzzers draw 25–40 mA, and the Arduino per-pin recommended limit is 20 mA) needs a transistor driver, the same as a loud buzzer.

where: Section 2, first paragraph and Quiz Q1
problem: The step size is given as 5 V ÷ 1024 while the conversion formula used everywhere (and in Q3) is V = reading × 5 ÷ 1023. Both numbers appear without explanation, so a student will not see why they differ and may mix them up.
fix: State clearly: there are 1024 steps (2¹⁰) across the reference, so one step is Vref ÷ 1024 ≈ 4.9 mV; the code formula V = reading × Vref ÷ 1023 maps the largest reading 1023 to full scale. Use one convention consistently, or explain why both appear.
